sentences.text:
It is submitted by learned counsel appearing for the appellant/convict that initially the FIR for the occurrence was lodged against unknown persons but during the course of trial, PW-2, namely,
Dinesh Ravidas testified that he came to know Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.2599 of 2023(4)
dt.11-12-2024 that occurrence was committed by this appellant/convict.

It also transpires from the testimony of PW-6/victim that the appellant was already known to her, as she not appears confused regrading name of this appellant while deposing before the court but, surprisingly, the FIR was lodged against unknown.

It is submitted that no injury was found in or around the private part of the victim and her hymen was also found intact and by taking advantage of the fact as victim received facial injury due to fall, the present false case of rape was lodged against the appellant.
In this context, it is pointed out that PW-7, who is a doctor and examined the victim/PW-6 categorically stated that the injury received by victim may cause due to falling on hard and blunt surface.

It is submitted that PW-2 is none but the uncle of the victim but, PW-6/victim categorically denied to have any relation with PW-2.
4.
It is also pointed out that the reason for false implication was land dispute, as it transpires from the testimony of PW-4.

It is submitted that in view of aforesaid background, the learned trial court disbelieved the version of rape particularly in terms of the medical report as opined by PW-7.
5.

While concluding argument, it is submitted that in Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.2599 of 2023(4) dt.11-12-2024 view of aforesaid fact, the balance of appeal appears in favour of appellant,
wherein appellant remains in custody for about two years and eight months against fixed term sentence of seven years, where this appeal is of June 2023 itself, which is not likely to be taken on Board for final hearing in near future and accordingly, on this ground alone, the appellant/convict deserves bail.

In support of his submission, learned counsel has placed reliance on a Full Bench judgment of this Court as passed in the matter of Anurag Baitha vs. State of Bihar [AIR 1987 Pat 274 (FB)] and also a judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court as passed in the matter of Atul @ Ashutosh vs.
State of Madhya Pradesh [(2024) 3 SCC 663].
6.

As far allegation qua SC/ST (POA) Act is concerned, it is submitted by learned counsel that even from testimony of PW-6 and other prosecution witnesses, it nowhere appears that occurrence took place out of atrocities as defined within the meaning of the Act and, therefore, the judgment of conviction as recorded by learned trial court for the offence committed under the Act appears questionable.
7.
Mrs. Usha Kumari-1, learned Special Public Prosecutor while opposing the prayer of bail and suspension of Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.2599 of 2023(4) dt.11-12-2024 sentence submitted that the victim has categorically testified during the trial that the appellant committed rape upon her.
However, she could not disputed the factual submissions including the custody period as submitted by learned counsel for the appellant.

Considering the fact that the testimony of victim/PW-6 if read in totality makes a prima facie doubt qua being a sterling witness to crime in question, coupled with the fact that appellant/convict remains in custody for about two years and eight months against fixed term sentence of seven years,
where appeal is of June, 2024 itself and same is not likely to be taken up for final hearing in near future, accordingly, the appellant/convict, above-named, is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned 1st A.D.J.-cum-Special Judge, SC/ST, Katihar/concerned court in S.T. No.410 of 2013 arising out of Dandkhora P.S. Case No.52 of 2012, during the pendency of appeal.
9. The sentence of imprisonment imposed by the learned trial court against the appellant/convict shall remain Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.2599 of 2023(4) dt.11-12-2024 suspended till disposal of the appeal.
Realization of fine, if any, shall also be kept in abeyance, during the pendency of appeal.
10. The appellant/convict is directed to co-operate in final hearing of appeal.

11. Observations, as regard to merit of the case, if any, shall be of no bearing while final hearing of the appeal, being prima facie observation.
12.
